q:
For positive non-zero real variables x and y, if
ln((x + y)/2) = (1/2)[ln(x) + ln(y)]
then, the value of x/y + y/x is
explanation: The equation says the arithmetic mean of x and y equals their geometric mean, √(xy), which forces x = y. Substituting x = y gives x/y + y/x = 1 + 1 = 2, matching the official key (C).

The number in a cell represents the count of the immediate neighboring cells (left, right, top, bottom, diagonals) NOT having a cross (X). Given that the last row has no crosses (X), the sum of the four numbers to be filled in the last row is

q: Which one of the following regular expressions is equivalent to the language accepted by the DFA given below?
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 170" width="100%" style="max-width:380px;height:auto" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="ah-2024s2cs22" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" refX="6" refY="3.5" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L7,3.5 L0,7 Z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><g fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4"><line x1="10" y1="90" x2="55" y2="90" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs22)"/><circle cx="75" cy="90" r="20"/><circle cx="225" cy="90" r="20"/><circle cx="225" cy="90" r="15"/><path d="M60,75 C55,45 90,45 88,73" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs22)"/><path d="M212,75 C207,45 242,45 240,73" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs22)"/><path d="M92,80 C140,45 175,45 210,78" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs22)"/><path d="M208,100 C160,135 130,135 92,102" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs22)"/></g><g font-size="12" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" text-anchor="middle"><text x="72" y="35">0</text><text x="222" y="35">0</text><text x="150" y="55">1</text><text x="150" y="150">1</text></g></svg>
explanation: The DFA has a non-accepting start state and an accepting state, each with a self-loop on 0 and cross-edges on 1 that flip between the two states, so a string is accepted exactly when it contains an odd number of 1's. This language is generated by 0*1(0 + 10*1)*, matching the official key (A).

q:
Consider the following context-free grammar where the start symbol is S and the set of terminals is {a,b,c,d}.
S → AaAb | BbBa
A → cS | ε
B → dS | ε

The following is a partially-filled LL(1) parsing table.

         a           b           c        d          $
S   S→AaAb      S→BbBa       (1)        (2)
A   A→ε           (3)        A→cS
B    (4)         B→ε                   B→dS

Which one of the following options represents the CORRECT combination for the numbered cells in the parsing table? ("blank" denotes an empty cell)
explanation: FIRST(AaAb) = FIRST(A)·{a} ∪ ... includes c (from A→cS) and a (from A→ε then literal a), so S→AaAb is entered under both a and c, giving cell (1) = S→AaAb; symmetrically S→BbBa must be entered under d, giving cell (2) = S→BbBa. Since FOLLOW(A) = {a} only (A is always immediately followed by literal a in both productions), A→ε is entered only under a, not b, so cell (3) is blank; similarly FOLLOW(B) = {b} only, so B→ε is not entered under a, leaving cell (4) blank too, matching the official key (A).

q: Let M be the 5-state NFA with ε-transitions shown in the diagram below. Which one of the following regular expressions represents the language accepted by M?
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 240" width="100%" style="max-width:380px;height:auto" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="ah-2024s2cs41" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" refX="6" refY="3.5" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L7,3.5 L0,7 Z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><g fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3"><line x1="10" y1="120" x2="45" y2="90" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs41)"/><circle cx="65" cy="70" r="20"/><circle cx="65" cy="70" r="15"/><circle cx="180" cy="70" r="20"/><circle cx="65" cy="170" r="20"/><circle cx="180" cy="170" r="20"/><circle cx="180" cy="170" r="15"/><line x1="60" y1="90" x2="60" y2="150" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs41)"/><path d="M85,63 C120,53 145,53 160,63" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs41)"/><path d="M160,80 C145,90 120,90 85,80" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs41)"/><line x1="180" y1="90" x2="180" y2="150" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs41)"/><path d="M85,163 C120,153 145,153 160,163" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs41)"/><path d="M160,180 C145,190 120,190 85,180" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs41)"/></g><g font-size="14" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" text-anchor="middle"><text x="65" y="75">2</text><text x="180" y="75">3</text><text x="65" y="175">4</text><text x="180" y="175">5</text><text x="30" y="105">1</text></g><g font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" text-anchor="middle"><text x="40" y="80">ε</text><text x="40" y="180">ε</text><text x="120" y="48">0</text><text x="120" y="102">0</text><text x="200" y="120">ε</text><text x="120" y="148">1</text><text x="120" y="202">1</text></g></svg>
explanation: Since ε-transitions are taken freely, any run of 0's (even or odd) starting from state 1 via state 2 eventually epsilon-reaches an accepting state, giving 0* as one accepted family; independently, an odd run of 1's via state 4 reaches accepting state 5, and any accepted 1-run or accepted odd 0-run can be followed by further (11)* pairs while staying accepting. This is exactly captured by 0* + (1 + 0(00)*)(11)*, matching the official key (B).

q:
Consider 4-variable functions f1, f2, f3, f4 expressed in sum-of-minterms form as given below.
f1 = Σ(0,2,3,5,7,8,11,13)
f2 = Σ(1,3,5,7,11,13,15)
f3 = Σ(0,1,4,11)
f4 = Σ(0,2,6,13)

With respect to the circuit given above (f1 AND f2, and f3 OR f4, both feeding an XOR gate whose output is Y), which of the following options is/are CORRECT?
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 380 260" width="100%" style="max-width:420px;height:auto" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="ah-2024s2cs50" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" refX="6" refY="3.5" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L7,3.5 L0,7 Z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><g fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3"><line x1="60" y1="45" x2="120" y2="45" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs50)"/><line x1="60" y1="75" x2="120" y2="75" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs50)"/><path d="M120,25 h40 a30,35 0 0 1 0,70 h-40 Z"/><line x1="60" y1="175" x2="115" y2="175" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs50)"/><line x1="60" y1="205" x2="115" y2="205" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs50)"/><path d="M115,155 q45,10 45,35 q0,25 -45,35 q12,-35 0,-70 Z"/><line x1="190" y1="60" x2="230" y2="60"/><line x1="230" y1="60" x2="230" y2="115" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs50)"/><line x1="160" y1="190" x2="230" y2="190"/><line x1="230" y1="190" x2="230" y2="135" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs50)"/><path d="M255,105 q50,15 50,20 q0,5 -50,20 q14,-20 0,-40 Z"/><line x1="335" y1="125" x2="365" y2="125" marker-end="url(#ah-2024s2cs50)"/></g><g font-size="13" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"><text x="30" y="49">f1</text><text x="30" y="79">f2</text><text x="30" y="179">f3</text><text x="30" y="209">f4</text><text x="132" y="65">AND</text><text x="135" y="195">OR</text><text x="280" y="130">XOR</text><text x="355" y="115">Y</text></g></svg>
explanation: f1 AND f2 = Σ(3,5,7,11,13); f3 OR f4 = Σ(0,1,2,4,6,11,13). XORing these sets (symmetric difference) removes their common minterms {11,13} and keeps the rest, giving Y = Σ(0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7). Since Π(8,...,15) denotes the complementary maxterm list for exactly this same set, options C and D describe the identical function, matching the official key (C, D).

q: The number of distinct minimum-weight spanning trees of the following graph is ________
explanation: The four weight-1 edges (a-b, a-f, c-d, d-e) form no cycle and must all be in every minimum spanning tree, leaving two 3-vertex components {a,b,f} and {c,d,e} plus the isolated vertex g. The cheapest way to connect everything is two weight-2 edges through g — one of the 3 edges joining g to {a,b,f} and one of the 3 edges joining g to {c,d,e} — giving 3×3 = 9 minimum-weight spanning trees (total weight 8), matching the official key.

q: The chromatic number of a graph is the minimum number of colours used in a proper colouring of the graph. The chromatic number of the following graph is ________
explanation: Tracing every edge shows the eight vertices split into two sets of four (alternating around the octagon) with no edges inside either set and every vertex joined to all four vertices of the other set — that is, the graph is the complete bipartite graph K4,4. Any bipartite graph is 2-colourable (and, having edges, needs at least 2 colours), so the chromatic number is 2, matching the official key.
